value.body: A science degree about individuals, families and communities. It usually covers five areas — food and nutrition, human development and family studies, textiles and clothing, resource management, and extension and communication — with a specialisation in later years. ICAR's agricultural universities now call it Community Science. It leads to nutrition, child-development, textile, extension and teaching work, and to postgraduate study.

items.note: 4 years for B.Sc (Hons) Community Science at agricultural universities and for NEP Honours degrees

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12; many colleges prefer or require science, while some accept arts or commerce (rules vary). Central universities admit through CUET-UG; state universities and women's colleges often admit on Class 12 merit or a state test. Agricultural universities admit to B.Sc (Hons) Community Science through ICAR's quota (via CUET-UG) or a state entrance.

value.title: At a glance
items: Most students are women, and many colleges offering it are women's colleges.
ICAR's Fifth Deans' Committee recommended renaming it Community Science; several agricultural universities adopted the name around 2017 (as reported).
Your specialisation shapes your options: food and nutrition leads towards dietetics; human development towards early-childhood and social-sector work; textiles towards apparel and quality roles.
Common next steps are an M.Sc in a home science area, an M.Sc in Food & Nutrition, or a B.Ed for teaching.
